mainTopic: Wool and linen in ציצית; סכך that can become טמא; and the new משנה on flax for שבת lights and טומאת אהלים
overview: The amud continues the teaching of the תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל that an unspecified 'garment' in the תורה means wool or linen. The גמרא explains that this teaching limits ציצית to wool and linen. Without it, we might have followed רבא, who lets other materials be obligated too. רב אחא בריה דרבא then asks why the words 'אשר תכסה בה' should not add other materials, as 'או בגד' does for טומאה. רב אשי answers that those words include a blind person's garment, and a ברייתא explains why the blind person is included while a night garment is excluded. The גמרא adds that a verse about wool and linen can only add more wool and linen. Next, אביי shows that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר and סומכוס share the same idea about סכך that can become טמא. סומכוס's view follows his teacher רבי מאיר about when threads can become impure from נגעים. A new משנה teaches that among tree products only flax may be lit for שבת, and only flax becomes impure through טומאת אהלים. The גמרא proves from ספר יהושע that flax is called עץ. רבי אלעזר begins a גזירה שוה on the word אהל, which is finished on the next amud.

steps.title: The teaching comes to include ציצית
steps.stepSummary: The teaching that every unspecified 'garment' means wool and linen comes to include the laws of ציצית.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include ציצית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the earlier question of what the תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל's rule adds: it tells us that ציצית applies only to wool and linen garments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule says that any 'garment' the תורה mentions without detail means wool or linen. Here we learn that the rule's real purpose is the מצוה of ציצית. So only wool and linen garments are obligated מדאורייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: to include / to bring in (a new case)
the fringes on a four-cornered garment

phrases.english: To include ritual fringes.
phrases.notes: This finishes the answer to the earlier question: what does the rule 'garments are wool and linen' add?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question (on the previous amud) about what the תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל's rule includes.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rule teaches that ציצית applies only to garments of wool and linen.

steps.title: Why is this needed if the verses already show it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: the Torah already puts ציצית right next to the verse about wool and linen.
steps.simpleTranslation: About ציצית it is written openly: 'Do not wear שעטנז, wool and linen,' and right after it is written: 'You shall make twisted fringes for yourself'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks Step 1: why do we need a special rule to teach that ציצית is only for wool and linen, when the Torah already shows this clearly?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In דברים, the verse about ציצית comes right after the verse about wool and linen. From this closeness we can already learn that ציצית is about wool and linen garments. So the תנא's rule seems unnecessary for ציצית.

keyTerms.meaning: a forbidden mixture of wool and linen

phrases.english: Regarding ritual fringes, it is written explicitly:
'Do not wear diverse kinds, wool and linen,'
and it is written: 'You shall make for yourself twisted fringes'!
phrases.notes: דברים כב:יב. These two verses sit side by side (סמוכים).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the answer in Step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the תנא's rule is needed to teach that ציצית is only for wool and linen.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The closeness of the שעטנז verse and the ציצית verse already teaches this, so the rule adds nothing.

steps.title: We might have followed רבא
steps.stepSummary: The answer starts: without the rule, we might have followed רבא's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought to say like רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer: the rule is still needed, because otherwise we would follow רבא's approach. This step sets up the next lines, which explain what רבא said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim is that the closeness of the verses alone is not enough. רבא reads the verses in a way that lets other materials also be obligated. So the rule is needed to block that reading.

keyTerms.meaning: it would have entered your mind to say (a possible mistaken thought)

phrases.english: It could have entered your mind to say in accordance with Rava.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the answer to the challenge in Step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the rule is needed to rule out another possible reading of the verses.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We would have followed רבא and said that other materials can also be obligated in ציצית.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule teaches that only wool and linen are obligated (completed in Step 6).

steps.title: רבא points out two verses that seem to clash
steps.stepSummary: רבא shows a contradiction: one verse says the fringes match the corner, and another says they are wool and linen.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבא pointed out a contradiction. It is written 'the corner,' meaning the same type as the corner. And it is written 'wool and linen together.' How can both be true?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבא, who notices two verses that seem to say different things about what the fringes must be made of. This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'הכנף' suggests that the fringes must be the same material as the garment's corner, whatever it is. The closeness to 'צמר ופשתים יחדיו' suggests that fringes must be wool and linen. רבא asks how to fit these together.

keyTerms.meaning: the same type (material) as the corner
how can this be? (asking how to settle a contradiction)

phrases.english: As Rava raised a contradiction:
It is written: 'the corner,' meaning the same type as the corner.
And it is written: 'wool and linen together,'
phrases.notes: This verse is next to the ציצית verse in דברים.

phrases.english: How can this be?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the רבא mentioned in Step 3 by quoting his contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: How the two verses about the fringes' material fit together.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One verse says the fringes match the garment, and the other says wool and linen. These seem to clash.

steps.title: רבא's resolution: wool and linen work for everything
steps.stepSummary: רבא: wool and linen fringes work on any garment; other materials work only on a garment of their own type.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wool and linen fringes exempt the garment whether it is their type or not their type. Other materials exempt a garment of their own type, but do not exempt a garment not of their type.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא settles the contradiction by giving each verse its own job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'צמר ופשתים' teaches that wool and linen fringes work on every garment. 'מין כנף' teaches that other materials, such as silk, work only on a garment of the same material. This implies that garments of other materials are also obligated in ציצית.
steps.confusionAlert: 'פוטרין' here does not mean the garment is free from ציצית. It means these fringes fulfill the מצוה for that garment.

phrases.english: Wool and linen fringes exempt the garment
whether it is of their type or not of their type.
Other types of material exempt a garment of their own type;
a garment not of their type, they do not exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's contradiction from Step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the verses: each one covers a different case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two verses seem to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Wool and linen fringes work on any garment, while other materials work only on their own type.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבא's view assumes that garments of other materials are obligated in ציצית. That is exactly the view the תנא's rule comes to reject.

steps.title: So the rule is needed to reject רבא's reading
steps.stepSummary: Because we might have followed רבא, the תנא teaches that only wool and linen are obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought like רבא; so it teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer to Step 2: the rule of the תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל is needed so that we do not follow רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The closeness of the verses alone could be read the way רבא reads it, which allows other materials. The general rule that 'garment' means wool and linen settles the matter. Only wool and linen garments are obligated מדאורייתא.
steps.whatToRemember: According to the תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל, only wool and linen garments are obligated in ציצית. The rule is needed because otherwise we might follow רבא and include other materials.

phrases.english: It would have entered your mind to follow Rava;
therefore it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ כִּדְרָבָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Wraps up the answer that began in Step 3.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The תנא's rule is needed to reject רבא's reading and limit ציצית to wool and linen.

steps.title: Why not include other garments as with impurity
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא asks: for טומאה we add other garments from 'או בגד'. Why not add them for ציצית from 'אשר תכסה בה'?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רבא said to רב אשי: According to the תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל, what is different about טומאה, where he includes other garments because it says 'or a garment'? Here too, let us include other garments from 'with which you cover yourself'!
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge: if the Torah adds other materials for the laws of טומאה, why not add them for ציצית too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even the תנא agrees that the extra words 'או בגד' bring other materials into the laws of טומאה. The ציצית verse also has extra words, 'אשר תכסה בה'. So those words should likewise add other materials.

keyTerms.meaning: that he includes (adds through an extra word)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha, son of Rava, said to Rav Ashi:
According to the tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael,
what is different about the matter of ritual impurity
that he includes other garments,
because it is written: 'or a garment'?
phrases.notes: ויקרא יא:לב. The extra word 'או' adds more.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי לֵימָא לְרַבּוֹת שְׁאָר בְּגָדִים
phrases.english: Here too, let us say it comes to include other garments
from 'with which you cover yourself'!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge to the conclusion that ציצית is limited to wool and linen.
steps.kashyaTarget: Limiting ציצית to wool and linen according to the תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An extra phrase adds other garments for טומאה, so the extra phrase in ציצית should add them too.

steps.title: That phrase includes a blind person's garment
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי: 'אשר תכסה בה' is needed for something else: to include a blind person's garment.
steps.simpleTranslation: That phrase comes to include the garment of a blind person.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers that the extra phrase is already 'used up' for a different purpose, so it cannot add other materials.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An extra phrase can teach only one thing. Here it teaches that a blind person's garment needs ציצית, even though he cannot see it. The next step brings the source for this.

phrases.english: That phrase is to include the garment of a blind person;
that is what it comes for.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהוּא לְאֵתוּיֵי כְּסוּת סוֹמֵא הוּא דַּאֲתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אחא's challenge in Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The phrase is needed for a different teaching.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אשר תכסה בה' adds garments of other materials.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אשר תכסה בה' adds a blind person's garment.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows the phrase includes a blind person
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: 'וראיתם אותו' excludes a night garment, while 'אשר תכסה בה' includes a blind person's garment.
steps.simpleTranslation: As was taught: 'And you shall see it' excludes a night garment. Do you say it excludes a night garment, or maybe it only excludes a blind person's garment? When it says 'with which you cover yourself,' a blind person's garment is already mentioned. So how do I fulfill 'and you shall see it'? It excludes a night garment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove רב אשי's point that 'אשר תכסה בה' is used for a blind person's garment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'וראיתם אותו' suggests that ציצית is only for something that can be seen. That could exclude either a night garment or a blind person's garment. Since 'אשר תכסה בה' covers anyone who wears a garment, the blind person is included, and 'וראיתם' excludes only the night garment.

keyTerms.meaning: how do I fulfill (what is this verse for)?

phrases.english: As it was taught: 'And you shall see it'
comes to exclude a night garment.
Do you say it excludes a night garment,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא פְּרָט לִכְסוּת סוֹמֵא?
phrases.english: or is it only to exclude the garment of a blind person?
When it says 'with which you cover yourself,'
the garment of a blind person is mentioned.
So how do I fulfill 'and you shall see it'?
It excludes a night garment.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא וּרְאִיתֶם אוֹתוֹ פְּרָט לִכְסוּת לַיְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב אשי's answer in Step 8 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That 'אשר תכסה בה' is used to include a blind person's garment.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that explains 'וראיתם אותו' and 'אשר תכסה בה'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the basis for the halacha that a blind person is obligated in ציצית, while a 'night garment' is exempt. ראשונים disagree about whether that means a garment made for nighttime wear or any garment worn at night.

steps.title: Why include the blind and exclude the night garment
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks: why include the blind person's garment and exclude the night garment, and not the other way around?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what did you see to include a blind person and to exclude a night garment?
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the ברייתא, a question is asked: one verse includes and one excludes, so how do we know which case goes where? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases no one wearing the garment can see the fringes. So it is fair to ask why the blind person is the one included. Maybe the night garment should be included and the blind person excluded.

keyTerms.meaning: what did you see (what is your reason)?

phrases.english: And what did you see to include a blind person
and to exclude a night garment?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the split made in Step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The logic for deciding which garment is included and which is excluded.

steps.title: Others can see the blind person's fringes
steps.stepSummary: A blind person's fringes can be seen by others, but a night garment cannot be seen even by others.
steps.simpleTranslation: I include a blind person's garment because others can see it, and I exclude a night garment because others cannot see it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers: 'seeing' can also be done by other people, and that decides the matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blind person cannot see his fringes, but people around him can, so the idea of 'seeing' still applies. At night no one can see the fringes at all. That is why the night garment is the one excluded.

phrases.english: I include the garment of a blind person
because it is visible to others,
and I exclude a night garment
because it is not visible to others.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְרַבֶּה אֲנִי כְּסוּת סוֹמֵא שֶׁיֶּשְׁנָהּ בִּרְאִיָּיה אֵצֶל אֲחֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Seeing by others is enough. The blind person's garment is seen by others, and the night garment is seen by no one.

steps.title: Maybe the phrase includes other materials instead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks again: maybe 'אשר תכסה בה' comes to include other materials, not the blind person.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say it comes to include other garments!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on Step 8: why use the extra phrase for a blind person, rather than for garments of other materials?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase can teach only one thing. Why assume it teaches about the blind person and not about other materials? This brings back רב אחא's challenge in a sharper form.

phrases.english: But say it comes to include other garments?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רב אשי's answer (Step 8) and questions why the phrase is used for the blind person.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's use of 'אשר תכסה בה' for a blind person's garment.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The phrase could just as easily be used to add garments of other materials.

steps.title: A wool-and-linen verse adds only wool and linen
steps.stepSummary: Since the verse is talking about wool and linen, it makes sense that it adds more wool and linen, not other materials.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is logical: the verse is standing on wool and linen, so it includes wool and linen. Would it stand on wool and linen and include other garments?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that an addition must fit the topic of its verse. A verse about wool and linen can add another wool or linen case (the blind person's garment), but not a new material.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אשר תכסה בה' sits right next to 'צמר ופשתים'. An extra phrase stretches the law within its own subject, so it adds a new case of wool and linen. Adding other materials would go beyond the verse's subject, unlike 'או בגד' in the laws of טומאה.
steps.whatToRemember: According to the תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל, ציצית is only for wool and linen. 'אשר תכסה בה' includes a blind person's wool or linen garment, while 'וראיתם אותו' excludes a night garment.

phrases.english: It is logical: when the verse is standing on wool and linen,
it includes wool and linen.
Would it stand on wool and linen
and include other garments?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִסְתַּבְּרָא קָאֵי בְּצֶמֶר וּפִשְׁתִּים מְרַבֵּה צֶמֶר וּפִשְׁתִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 12 and closes the discussion of רב אחא's question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logic of context: an addition stays within the subject of its verse.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אשר תכסה בה' might add garments of other materials.
steps.terutzMaskana: It adds only more wool and linen cases, namely the blind person's garment.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The extra phrase in ציצית adds the blind person's garment, not other materials.

steps.title: אביי: Two Sages Said the Same Idea
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר and סומכוס hold the same position. For רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, we mean the ruling already discussed.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר and סומכוס said the same thing. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: that which we said earlier.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי makes a new statement connecting two sages. Then he points back to the ruling of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר that we already learned. This sets up the next step, where he shows us where סומכוס says it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי שמעון בן אלעזר disqualified even small cloths as סכך because they can become טמא. אביי claims another sage, סומכוס, holds the same principle. He does not repeat רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's words, because we already learned them ('הא דאמרן').

keyTerms.meaning: One thing, meaning the same idea or ruling
That which we said already, pointing back to an earlier statement

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar and Sumakhos
said one and the same thing.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר הָא דַּאֲמַרַן.
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar: that which we already said.
phrases.notes: Refers to his earlier ruling about small cloths as סכך.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר וְסוֹמְכוֹס אָמְרוּ דָּבָר אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the earlier opinion of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר after the ציצית discussion, and links it to another sage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר and סומכוס share the principle that material able to become טמא is disqualified as סכך.

steps.title: סומכוס Disqualifies Spun Thread as סוכה Roofing
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows the opinion of סומכוס. A סוכה roofed with spun thread is פסול, because spun thread can become impure from נגעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: סומכוס: as it was taught in a ברייתא, סומכוס says: If one roofed a סוכה with spun thread, it is disqualified, because it can become impure from נגעים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for סומכוס's side of אביי's comparison. סומכוס says spun thread cannot be used as סכך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reason is that spun thread can already become טמא through נגעים, the 'leprosy' of garments. This is the same logic as רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: if something can become טמא, it may not be used as סכך. This proves אביי's claim that both sages said 'one thing.'

keyTerms.meaning: He roofed it, meaning put סכך on the סוכה
Spun thread (thread that has been spun but not yet woven)
Spots of צרעת, which can also make garments טמא

steps.confusionAlert: Be careful: 'נגעים' here is not about a person's skin. It is the צרעת of garments, which applies to wool and linen. The question is whether even thread, before it is woven, can get this impurity.

phrases.english: Sumakhos: as it was taught in a baraita:
Sumakhos says: if he roofed it with spun thread, it is disqualified
because it can become impure from leprosy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for סומכוס's half of אביי's comparison.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that סומכוס holds the same principle as רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting סומכוס: spun thread used as סכך is פסול because it can become impure from נגעים.

steps.title: Whose View Does סומכוס Follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which earlier תנא holds, like סומכוס, that spun thread can already become impure from נגעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: In accordance with whom?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short clarifying question. Which opinion is סומכוס following? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is not obvious that plain spun thread, not yet woven into a garment, can become impure from נגעים. So the גמרא wants to find a תנא in a משנה who says this.

keyTerms.meaning: Like whom? Which opinion does this follow?

phrases.english: In accordance with whom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the background opinion behind סומכוס's assumption in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that spun thread can become impure from נגעים.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: Warp and Woof Become Impure Right Away
steps.stepSummary: סומכוס follows רבי מאיר. In a משנה, רבי מאיר says warp and woof threads can become impure from נגעים immediately.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like this תנא, as we learned in a משנה: Warp and woof can become impure from נגעים immediately; these are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that סומכוס follows רבי מאיר. It quotes a משנה where רבי מאיר says threads can become טמא from נגעים right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Warp (שתי) and woof (ערב) are the two sets of threads used in weaving. רבי מאיר says they can become impure 'מיד,' as soon as they are spun, without further processing. This makes sense because סומכוס was רבי מאיר's student.

keyTerms.meaning: Warp, the lengthwise threads on a loom
Woof, the crosswise threads woven through the warp

phrases.english: Like this tanna, as we learned in a mishna:
Warp and woof become impure from leprosy immediately,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question 'כמאן' by naming רבי מאיר.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: סומכוס follows רבי מאיר, who says warp and woof threads can become impure from נגעים immediately after spinning.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: Each Thread Becomes Impure at a Different Stage
steps.stepSummary: In the same משנה, רבי יהודה disagrees. Warp becomes impure only after it is taken out of the boiling pot, and woof right away. Raw flax bundles become impure only after they are bleached.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה says: The warp, after it is removed from the boiling; and the woof, immediately; and bundles of flax, after they are bleached.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה with רבי יהודה's opposing view. This shows that סומכוס's ruling fits רבי מאיר and not רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, warp threads are not finished enough to become טמא until they have been boiled and taken out of the pot. Woof threads become impure right away. Bundles of raw flax become impure only after bleaching. So for רבי יהודה, not all spun thread is immediately susceptible. That is why סומכוס's flat rule matches רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: From when it is taken out (of the boiling pot)

steps.whatToRemember: סומכוס disqualifies spun thread as סכך because it can become טמא. That only works according to רבי מאיר, his teacher, who says warp and woof become impure immediately. רבי יהודה requires more processing.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda says:
the warp, from when it is removed from the boiling; and the woof, immediately;
and bundles of flax, from when they are bleached.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quoted משנה with the dissenting view, which sharpens why סומכוס matches רבי מאיר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: warp becomes impure only after boiling, woof immediately, and raw flax bundles only after bleaching.

steps.title: משנה: Flax Is the Exception Among Tree Products
steps.stepSummary: New משנה: among everything that comes from a tree, only flax may be used for שבת lighting. Also, only flax becomes impure through טומאת אהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Of everything that comes from a tree, one may not light with it except flax. And of everything that comes from a tree, none becomes impure with tent impurity except flax.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, still in the same chapter about שבת lights. It teaches two rules where flax is the one exception among plant materials.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First rule: plant-based wicks may not be used for שבת lights, except flax, because the others do not burn well. Second rule: if a tent is made of plant material and a dead body is inside, the tent itself does not become טמא, except a tent of flax (linen). In both cases flax is treated as a 'tree product,' which sets up the גמרא's question.

keyTerms.meaning: What comes from a tree, meaning plant-based material
Impurity of tents, where a tent over a dead body becomes טמא

steps.confusionAlert: The second rule is about the tent material itself becoming טמא. Everything under any tent with a dead body becomes טמא. The משנה is saying that only a flax tent is itself impure.

phrases.english: Mishna:
Everything that comes from a tree
one may not light with it, except flax.
And everything that comes from a tree

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ מִטַּמֵּא טוּמְאַת אֹהָלִים, אֶלָּא פִּשְׁתָּן.
phrases.english: does not become impure with tent impurity, except flax.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הַיּוֹצֵא מִן הָעֵץ אֵין מַדְלִיקִין בּוֹ, אֶלָּא פִּשְׁתָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the previous discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Of all tree products, only flax may be used for Shabbat lighting, and only flax becomes impure through טומאת אהלים.

steps.title: How Do We Know Flax Is Called a Tree?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that flax is called עץ, since it does not look like a tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we know that flax is called 'tree'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking about a word in the משנה. Why does the משנה count flax as something 'from a tree'? The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Flax is a thin plant, not a tree. The משנה's phrase 'except flax' assumes flax belongs to the 'tree' category. So the גמרא asks for a source in פסוק that calls flax עץ.

phrases.english: Gemara:
From where do we know that flax is called a 'tree'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the assumption in the משנה that flax is a tree product.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that flax is called עץ.

steps.title: מר זוטרא: The Verse Says 'Flax of the Tree'
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא quotes the verse about רחב hiding the spies 'בפשתי העץ,' which calls flax עץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: Because the verse says: 'And she had brought them up to the roof and hid them in the stalks of flax (literally, flax of the tree).'
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא answers with a פסוק from ספר יהושע. רחב hid the spies under 'פשתי העץ,' meaning 'flax of the tree.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse literally joins flax with the word עץ. This shows that the language of the פסוק counts flax as a 'tree' product. That explains why the משנה lists flax as the exception among things that come from a tree.
steps.whatToRemember: Flax counts as 'from the tree' because the verse in יהושע calls it 'פשתי העץ.'

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said: because the verse said:
'And she had brought them up to the roof
and hid them in the flax of the tree.'
phrases.notes: יהושע ב:ו, about רחב hiding the spies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מנלן question with a verse.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse in יהושע calls flax 'פשתי העץ,' showing flax is called עץ.

steps.title: Asking for the source of the flax tent rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that only flax, among tree products, becomes impure through טומאת אהלים, and asks where we learn it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the משנה said: of everything that comes from a tree, nothing becomes impure through tent-impurity except flax. Where do we learn this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the second rule from the משנה and asks for its source. This sets up the next step, where רבי אלעזר will answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא already found a verse calling flax 'עץ' (Step 21), which explains why flax counts as a tree product. Now it needs a separate source for the second rule: why flax, and nothing else from a tree, becomes impure when used as a tent over a dead body.

keyTerms.meaning: Tent-impurity: the impurity that spreads from a dead body to things under the same roof or cover
Whatever comes from a tree (plant materials)
From where do we know this? (a request for a source)

steps.confusionAlert: Here טומאת אהלים means the material itself becomes impure when it is spread as a tent over a dead body. The question is about which materials can become impure this way. It is not about which materials block or carry impurity to others.

phrases.english: And whatever comes from a tree
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the משנה again (see Step 19).

phrases.english: does not become impure with tent-impurity,
except flax.
From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the source for flax being called עץ (the first rule), the גמרא moves to the second rule of the same משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source showing that, of all tree products, only flax becomes impure through טומאת אהלים.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר links the word 'tent' in two places
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers that the rule is learned through a גזירה שוה built on the word אהל, which appears in two places in the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: we learn it by comparing the word 'tent' here with the word 'tent' there.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר starts to answer with a word-link between two תורה passages that both use the word אהל. The amud ends in the middle of his answer, and the next amud names the two verses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה lets us carry a detail from one passage over to another passage that uses the same word. One אהל is in the laws of a dead body in a tent. The other is the אהל of the משכן, which was made of flax (linen). So the 'tent' that becomes impure must be the same kind of material as the משכן's tent, which is flax.

keyTerms.meaning: He learned (one thing from another), here through a word-link
A word-link: the same word in two Torah passages lets us apply a detail from one to the other

steps.whyThisMatters: This is why the rule in the משנה is limited to flax. The definition of a 'tent' for impurity comes from the משכן's tent, not from general logic.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
He learned 'tent' from 'tent'
phrases.notes: This is a גזירה שוה. The two verses are given on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מנלן question of Step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is a גזירה שוה on the word אהל, linking the laws of a dead body in a tent to the tent of the משכן, which was made of flax. The answer is completed on the next amud.
